tagline: D.R. Horton, Inc. is the largest homebuilding company in the United States as measured by number of homes closed.
hero_kpi_rationale: The number of homes closed is the primary indicator of DHI's activity and size, reflecting its position as the undisputed leader in the U.S. residential construction market.
company_description: D.R. Horton, Inc. operates as a homebuilding company in East, North, Southeast, South Central, Southwest, and Northwest regions in the United States. It engages in the acquisition and development of land; and construction and sale of residential homes in 126 markets across 36 states under the names of D.R. Horton. The company also constructs and sells single-family detached homes; and attached homes, such as townhomes and duplexes. In addition, it provides mortgage financing and title agency services; and engages in the residential lot development business. Further, the company develops, constructs, owns, leases, and sells multi-family and single-family rental properties; conducts insurance-related operations; and owns water rights and other water-related assets, as well as non-residential real estate, including ranch land and improvements. It primarily serves homebuyers. D.R. Horton, Inc. was founded in 1978 and is headquartered in Arlington, Texas.

kpis.name: Homes Closed
kpis.explanation: Total number of homes sold and delivered by the company during a fiscal year.
kpis.description: This KPI measures the volume of finalized sales, reflecting the company's ability to meet housing market demand.
kpis.signal: Key volume indicator for residential construction activity.

kpis.name: Homebuilding Revenues
kpis.explanation: Revenue generated by the core homebuilding and home sales business.
kpis.description: Represents the majority of the company's revenue, directly linked to sales volume and home prices.
kpis.signal: Reflects the financial performance of the core business.

kpis.name: Consolidated Revenues
kpis.explanation: Total company revenue, including all business activities.
kpis.description: Encompasses revenues from construction, rental, and financial services, providing an overall view of business activity.
kpis.signal: Global indicator of the company's size and growth.

kpis.name: Pre-tax Operating Margin
kpis.explanation: Company profitability before taxes, expressed as a percentage of revenues.
kpis.description: Indicates the margin generated from ongoing operations, before tax deductions.
kpis.signal: Measures operational efficiency before tax impact.

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.explanation: Final profit after all expenses and taxes.
kpis.description: Represents the actual profit distributed to shareholders or reinvested in the company.

kpis.name: Diluted EPS
kpis.explanation: Profit attributable to each outstanding common share, after dilution.
kpis.description: Indicates the portion of net income attributable to each share, accounting for potentially dilutive shares.

kpis.name: Net Cash from Operations
kpis.explanation: Cash generated by the company's core operating activities.
kpis.description: Shows the cash available from ongoing operations, essential for financing, investment, and debt repayment.
kpis.signal: Key indicator of the company's ability to generate cash.

kpis.name: Return on Equity
kpis.explanation: Measures the return generated on shareholders' invested equity.
kpis.description: Evaluates how effectively the company uses shareholder funds to generate profits.

kpis.name: Home Sales Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Gross margin specific to home sales activity, before other expenses.
kpis.description: Measures the margin realized on home sales, influenced by construction costs and selling prices.
kpis.signal: Key indicator of direct profitability from home sales.

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.description: Annual consolidated revenue, values extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL for the last 8 fiscal years from 10-K filings.
kpis.signal: Revenue of $34.25B in the most recent year.

kpis.name: Average Closing Price
kpis.explanation: Average price at which homes were sold during the fiscal year.
kpis.description: This KPI reflects the average value of homes sold, influenced by property type and market conditions.
kpis.signal: Indicates housing price trends and product positioning.

kpis.name: Lots Controlled Through Purchase Contracts
kpis.explanation: Percentage of lots with acquisition secured through purchase contracts.
kpis.description: Shows the proportion of land the company has secured control over, reducing future supply risk.
kpis.signal: Indicator of land inventory management strategy.

kpis.short: Homes closed on lots developed by Forestar or third party
kpis.name: Homes Closed on Lots Developed by Forestar or Third Party
kpis.explanation: Percentage of homes closed on lots developed by external partners or Forestar.
kpis.description: Measures the use of lots from Forestar (subsidiary) or other developers, reflecting the land sourcing strategy.
kpis.signal: Indicates reliance on and collaboration with external developers.

risks.title: Construction Defect Claims
risks.summary: DHI faces approximately 875 construction defect claims, with 455 new claims in 2025. Resolution costs could exceed current estimates and significantly impact future results.
risks.score_rationale: Risk positioned mid-report with moderate language ('could significantly change'). Stable trend but growing volume (875 vs 825 claims). Litigation category weighted heavily for homebuilder. Quantified sensitivity: +10% = $155M impact.

risks.title: Housing Market Condition Volatility
risks.summary: Housing market fluctuations affect gross margins, absorption rates, and inventory valuations. DHI must regularly reassess its communities to detect potential impairments.
risks.score_rationale: Risk mid-report with strong language ('could significantly change'). Stable trend but recognized as major uncertainty factor. Directly affects inventory valuations and margins. High macro weighting for homebuilder.

risks.title: Real Estate Inventory Impairment
risks.summary: DHI evaluates its communities quarterly to detect impairments. Future cash flow estimates depend on uncertain local factors (prices, costs, absorption). Estimation errors could require significant charges.
risks.score_rationale: Risk mid-report with moderate language ('could differ'). Stable trend but complex estimation process subject to revision. Strong capital weighting: inventory represents major asset. Many local factors impact valuation.

risks.title: Interest Rate Risk on Debt
risks.summary: DHI is exposed to interest rate risk on its long-term debt. Rate changes affect the fair value of fixed-rate debt and future cash flows on variable-rate debt, particularly during refinancing.
risks.score_rationale: Risk positioned late in report (Item 7A) with moderate language ('may affect'). Stable trend. Strong credit weighting but DHI uses fixed/variable debt mix. Limited impact on fixed debt until refinancing.

risks.title: Interest Rate Risk on Mortgage Operations
risks.summary: DHI originates mortgage loans and resells them. It is exposed to interest rate risk through interest rate lock commitments (IRLC). It uses forward MBS sales for hedging.
risks.score_rationale: Risk positioned late in report with neutral language ('manage through hedging'). Stable trend. Moderate credit weighting for secondary mortgage activity. DHI uses hedges (MBS forward sales) to mitigate.

risks.title: Insurance Reserve Uncertainty
risks.summary: DHI is largely self-insured for construction defect claims. Estimates for recovery from insurers and subcontractors are subject to significant variability and judgment.
risks.score_rationale: Risk mid-report with moderate language ('could differ significantly'). Stable trend but acknowledges significant self-insurance (high retentions). Moderate credit weighting. High variability due to external factors (insurer practices, legal interpretations).
